news.full_article_text: Manipur police arrest 13, including a minor for circulating non-consensual explicit videos of women A suo motu case was registered under relevant sections of the Information Technology Act, Pocso Act, and BNS Manipur police arrested 13 people, including a minor, for allegedly circulating and monetising non-consensual explicit videos and photographs of local women, including child sexual abuse material (CSAM), through multiple Telegram channels and WhatsApp groups, police said on Tuesday. A senior police officer on Tuesday said that the accused were arrested on Monday night following an investigation under Operation Dignity, which was launched after the police received credible information about channels allegedly involved in circulating such material, including CSAM. A suo motu case was registered under relevant sections of the Information Technology Act, the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). During the investigation, a police team led by Leishangthem Jeebit Singh, sub-divisional police officer (SDPO) of Moirang in Bishnupur district, recovered and seized 14 mobile phones and a laptop allegedly used to commit the offences. Also Read: Manipur hill districts remain tense after Kamjong clashes, bodies of victims handed to kin The investigation revealed that Telegram channels and WhatsApp groups were allegedly being used to distribute sexually explicit content, with access sold to subscribers. Many of the clips reportedly featured women from Manipur who had not consented to their distribution. A police statement said, “The investigation indicates the network is organised, profit-driven, and self-sustaining, with subscriber demand encouraging further recording and release.” According to the statement, administrators used teaser previews on open platforms to attract subscribers, charging between ₹ 150 and ₹ 500 through digital payment platforms before providing access to private groups. A senior police officer, requesting anonymity, told HT that the investigation had uncovered “an organised secondary market fuelled by non-consensual leaks, hacking, and in several instances, direct production and grave non-consensual sexual exploitation by the accused”. The officer said the police identified more than 150 active Telegram channels and WhatsApp groups and had neutralised 38 of them. “We have recovered more than 6,000 video clips, and many of them were found to have been captured using hidden cameras, AI-generated content and other means without the consent of the victims,” the officer said. “It was also found that most of the videos were taken using hidden cameras and mobile phones in restrooms, hotels and changing rooms,” the officer added. The officer said most of the accused were college students, school dropouts, labourers and employees of private institutions. The officer added that more people could be involved in the alleged crimes. “As the investigation is underway, no further information can be provided about the accused or victims,” the officer said. The arrested persons have been identified as N Rajesh Singh alias Maipakchao (21), from Bishnupur; H Dhanajit Singh alias Taison (19), from Bishnupur; S Saphaba Singh (19), from Imphal West; Th Cavendish Singh alias Ingocha (21), from Kakching; H Rojit Singh (19), from Bishnupur; M Clinton Singh (28), from Bishnupur; Kh Bipin Singh (31), from Thoubal; S Simpson Singh (34), from Imphal West; A Aria Singh (24), from Bishnupur; S Alexander Singh (31), from Kakching; K Rakesh Singh (18), from Imphal West; Ch Robert Singh (27), from Imphal West; and one child in conflict with the law. The police statement said the investigation was underway to establish the wider network, trace financial transactions and identify additional victims. In an advisory issued on Tuesday, Bishnupur police warned the public against possessing, circulating, forwarding or hosting non-consensual intimate media and CSAM, stating that such acts could attract criminal prosecution under applicable laws. The police also cautioned that paying subscription fees to access private groups did not guarantee anonymity and that subscribers could face prosecution if found to be involved in the alleged network. The public has been urged not to forward teaser clips, previews or group links and to report offending accounts and links to the police. Parents and guardians have been advised to monitor children’s online activities, particularly on Telegram and WhatsApp, and encourage them to report uncomfortable behaviour, unauthorised image leaks, hacking or online blackmail. The police assured victims that their identities will remain protected in accordance with statutory requirements. They also said assistance will be provided to facilitate content removal through StopNCII and platform-level takedown mechanisms, along with access to legal aid, trauma counselling and state victim compensation support. The statement further warned that investigators were tracing digital evidence, including UPI transactions, bank accounts, QR payment records and device identifiers, to identify others allegedly involved in the network.

news.story_lead: Can new transport authority tackle siloed planning gaps? news.full_article_text: Can new transport authority tackle siloed planning gaps? India’s new transport authority aims to coordinate infrastructure planning, but experts say its impact hinges on real powers, reliable data and travel demand. Khajuraho Airport in Madhya Pradesh secured the joint top position in the Airports Authority of India’s customer satisfaction survey for January-June 2026, with a score of 4.98 out of 5. Incidentally, scheduled commercial flights from the airport stopped on July 1, before the survey results were out. The development illustrates the mismatch between infrastructure provision and actual travel demand, with experts describing the practice of planning and building transport infrastructure as individualised, tokenised projects rather than parts of a larger plan on journeys people and goods make. The Union Cabinet’s October 6 approval of the Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority (ITLA) has raised expectations among policy observers that India could move towards more coordinated planning of roads, railways, ports, aviation, waterways and urban mobility. The authority is mandated to prepare a National Transport Master Plan with a horizon of at least 10 years, and will test ministries’ annual and shorter-term sectoral plans against it. It will also appraise central infrastructure projects costing ₹ 500 crore or more, monitor their implementation and assess their impact after completion. Whether it can deliver, experts say, will turn on the powers it is given. A senior government official with experience across more than one transport-sector ministry at the Centre, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said departments often plan to expand their own networks without adequately accounting for investments being made by others. He said at different meetings within the government, the example of Japan’s Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism has been cited, which was created following a merger in 2001. “A railway line, highway or waterway may each be justified within its sector’s plans, but the connections between them can be overlooked. Everybody is trying to increase their own share from the same pie without looking at which is the most beneficial for the end user or the most resource-smart,” the official said. The result, the official said, can be overlapping projects and infrastructure that does not connect properly with the wider network. “First- and last-mile links are a particular weakness. For example, a freight terminal or railway station may be built without adequate road connectivity to bring goods or passengers to it.” Power, or the lack of it Without powers to halt funding for individual projects, ITLA’s influence remains uncertain. Jagan Shah, professor of practice at IIT Delhi’s Transportation Research and Injury Prevention Centre, said the authority would need veto powers to make its broad mandate effective. “Unless the authority has veto power — the mandate to review projects and, where necessary, veto them — it risks being unable to influence decisions,” Shah said, warning that a lack of powers, resources and independence could undermine both the public interest and the authority’s functioning. Shah also raised questions about how ITLA would work with state and local agencies, particularly development authorities, whose responsibilities could overlap with its planning mandate. He cited the UK’s National Infrastructure Commission as an example of an independent body that can publicly challenge the government on infrastructure decisions. Only as good as its data ITLA’s ability to compare projects will also depend on the quality of the information available to it. It is expected to build a National Transport Data Repository by bringing together data from Goods and Services Tax Network e-way bills, FASTag, VAHAN, global positioning systems and urban traffic management systems. The government says the repository will support freight-flow and origin-destination analysis for planning, monitoring and impact assessment. Shah said the repository would need to be regularly updated and access to its data governed transparently. If information is incomplete or accessible only to selected users, he warned, it would create uncompetitive markets that would hurt economic growth in the medium and long term. Pawan Mulukutla, executive programme director for integrated transport, clean air and hydrogen at WRI India, said the authority should include industry representatives and independent experts to ensure decisions reflect operational realities. “Different transport modes should complement rather than compete with one another, with choices guided by geography, the type of goods being moved, journey requirements, cost and efficiency.” He said all investment decisions must be tested against the economics of moving people and goods, with scope to use modelling and artificial intelligence-based tools to assess which transport modes would work best for particular routes and types of freight. Capex vs service-oriented approach The need for coordination has been recognised for years. Ravi Gadepalli, founder of Transit Intelligence, a public transport consultancy, said the idea of an integrated transport ministry has been around for a long time, “But it is difficult for institutions (different ministries) to give up independent decision-making powers.” Gadepalli hopes the ITLA can be a via-media solution where ministries retain their powers but coordinate on project specific matters. “The ILTA may go-beyond co-ordination and execute projects which are not within any individual ministry’s mandate such as building a multimodal hub connecting a railway station with a bus station, where separate agencies may have to build different components and secure permissions from one another.” For passenger transport, that means looking beyond new roads and rail infrastructure to how people actually travel between and within cities. “Transport sector spending remains skewed towards building infrastructure rather than providing services. Highways are treated as development expenditure, while buses and railways are often expected to recover their costs through fares, even when affordable services require continuing public funding support,” he said. To make the case for changing this approach, Gadepalli pointed to a 2020 policy brief by the International Association of Public Transport (UITP), which he co-authored. The study compared the employment and mobility benefits of different investments. India’s new transport authority aims to coordinate infrastructure planning, but experts say its impact hinges on real powers, reliable data and travel demand.

Khajuraho Airport in Madhya Pradesh secured the joint top position in the Airports Authority of India’s customer satisfaction survey for January-June 2026, with a score of 4.98 out of 5. Incidentally, scheduled commercial flights from the airport stopped on July 1, before the survey results were out.

The development illustrates the mismatch between infrastructure provision and actual travel demand, with experts describing the practice of planning and building transport infrastructure as individualised, tokenised projects rather than parts of a larger plan on journeys people and goods make.

The Union Cabinet’s October 6 approval of the Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority (ITLA) has raised expectations among policy observers that India could move towards more coordinated planning of roads, railways, ports, aviation, waterways and urban mobility.

The authority is mandated to prepare a National Transport Master Plan with a horizon of at least 10 years, and will test ministries’ annual and shorter-term sectoral plans against it. It will also appraise central infrastructure projects costing ₹ 500 crore or more, monitor their implementation and assess their impact after completion. Whether it can deliver, experts say, will turn on the powers it is given.

A senior government official with experience across more than one transport-sector ministry at the Centre, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said departments often plan to expand their own networks without adequately accounting for investments being made by others. He said at different meetings within the government, the example of Japan’s Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism has been cited, which was created following a merger in 2001.

“A railway line, highway or waterway may each be justified within its sector’s plans, but the connections between them can be overlooked. Everybody is trying to increase their own share from the same pie without looking at which is the most beneficial for the end user or the most resource-smart,” the official said.

Two Maldivian pilots working for flydubai have been arrested in the United Arab Emirates in connection with an alleged attempt to hijack and crash a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight, media reports said. The two pilots were taken into custody on October 3, and their families have been formally notified of their detention by the Maldivian Embassy in the UAE, Maldivian news portal Adhadhu reported. Authorities in the Maldives have not commented on the arrests. The UAE has also not released official details about the allegations against the two men or clarified whether investigators have established their involvement in the suspected plot. They are also reported to have lived in the same building as him. However, authorities have not disclosed the nature of their alleged links to the incident or the evidence, if any, against them. Reportedly, al-Hammami allegedly attacked Machchhar with an axe and stabbed him in an attempt to take control of the aircraft and carry out a "terrorist attack". Despite being seriously injured, Machchhar resisted the alleged assault and managed to unlock the cockpit door. Crew members and passengers then entered the cockpit, overpowered the co-pilot and helped stabilise the aircraft. The plane subsequently made an emergency landing at Tabuk airport in Saudi Arabia. Banerjee had come out of her house to inaugurate a Durga Puja pandal near her residence when the woman tried to enter the security cordon from behind. “When I asked her identity, she said that Banerjee was her paternal aunt. I refused to let her in. She then tried to sneak into the security cordon from the front. When she failed, she lay down on the road and started hurling abuses. It was then that we saw that she had a knife,” Sen said. A TMC leader said that the woman was overpowered by TMC workers around Banerjee and later handed over to the police. No senior police officials, including Rahul De, deputy commissioner of police (south), responded to calls and messages.

news.headline: 11 dead, several missing after boat capsizes in Bihar’s Raghopur
news.story_lead: 11 dead, several missing after boat capsizes in Bihar’s Raghopur Around 25 to 30 people were reportedly aboard the medium-sized boat, most of them travelling to attend a feast organised as part of Hindu funeral rituals. At least 11 people, all minors under the age of 18, have died and several others are missing after a boat capsized in the Ganga near Rampur Shyamchand village in Bihar’s Vaishali district on Tuesday evening. Vaishali District Magistrate Varsha Singh said seven people had been rescued, including the boat owner, and that rescue operations would continue through the night.
news.full_article_text: 11 dead, several missing after boat capsizes in Bihar’s Raghopur Around 25 to 30 people were reportedly aboard the medium-sized boat, most of them travelling to attend a feast organised as part of Hindu funeral rituals. At least 11 people, all minors under the age of 18, have died and several others are missing after a boat capsized in the Ganga near Rampur Shyamchand village in Bihar’s Vaishali district on Tuesday evening. Vaishali District Magistrate Varsha Singh said seven people had been rescued, including the boat owner, and that rescue operations would continue through the night. “According to the information we have so far, there were around 15 to 20 people on the boat. Of them, 11, all minors aged around 15, have died. Seven people, including the boat owner, have been rescued. We are carrying out rescue operations, which will continue throughout the night,” Singh said. Initial reports suggested that around 25 to 30 people were aboard the medium-sized boat, most of them travelling to attend a feast organised as part of Hindu funeral rituals. The boat was “ferrying passengers from one hamlet to another along the river” when it overturned, a senior police official told HT. Officials said the vessel capsized after becoming unbalanced, while some passengers managed to swim to safety. Locals who witnessed the incident rushed to help and alerted the administration. Several children were taken to a primary health centre by locals, where a doctor examined them and declared them dead. Their families were inconsolable, with relatives breaking down in tears. Singh said the boat was owned by a local resident who had used it to ferry villagers to a feast in a nearby village. “The boat owner has claimed there were 15 to 20 people on board. We are still verifying the facts,” she said. The district magistrate added that boat operations at night were restricted and that the incident would be investigated. Teams from the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) are searching the river for the missing passengers. Darkness and the depth of the water have hampered rescue efforts. Bihar CM announces ₹ 4 lakh ex gratia for kin Chief minister Samrat Choudhary, in an X post on his official handle, described the deaths of minors in boat capsize as heart-wrenching and saddening. The CM has announced that families of the deceased would be given ₹ four lakh each as ex gratia and has directed the administration to conduct rescue operations and ensure that the injured get best of medicare. Opposition leader Tejashwi Yadav in his official X handle described the incident as tragic and unfortunate. He wrote " tragic and unfortunate news has been received of a boat capsizing in the Raghopur Diara area. Most of those who drowned were children. May God keep everyone safe. A directive has been issued to coordinate with local people, the administration and officials to speed up relief, rescue and treatment operations". Yadav's represents the Raghopur assembly constituency, one of the riverine areas in Vaishali district. Boat capsized in Bihar’s Samastipur Earlier this year, at least three people died and four went missing after a boat carrying 14 passengers capsized in the Ganga near Sultanpur Diara in Bihar’s Samastipur district in May. Seven passengers were rescued safely, officials said. The passengers, all residents of Bind Toli in Masoomganj under Patna district’s Barh police station area, had travelled to Sultanpur Diara for agricultural work. They were returning to Umanath Ghat with vegetables harvested from parwal fields when the boat overturned. Mohiuddin Nagar circle officer Brijesh Kumar Dwivedi confirmed three deaths, saying the deceased included two men and one woman. Officials have established the identities of all three victims. The Patna district administration said the boat departed from Bind Toli around 5.45 am with 14 people on board. The passengers regularly crossed the river to work in agricultural fields. An initial update from the administration said seven people had been rescued, two bodies recovered and five passengers were missing. Officials cited strong winds as a possible cause of the accident, while Barh sub-divisional officer Garima Lohiya said the boat’s engine failed midstream. Rescue teams from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), along with the Patna and Samastipur district administrations, took part in the operation. As news of the accident spread, local residents and relatives gathered at Umanath Ghat. Authorities continued the search for the missing passengers and carried out procedures related to the recovered bodies. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Avinash Kumar Avinash, a senior correspondent, reports on crime, railways, defence and social sector, with specialisation in police, home department and other investigation agencies.

At least 11 people, all minors under the age of 18, have died and several others are missing after a boat capsized in the Ganga near Rampur Shyamchand village in Bihar’s Vaishali district on Tuesday evening.
Vaishali District Magistrate Varsha Singh said seven people had been rescued, including the boat owner, and that rescue operations would continue through the night.

“According to the information we have so far, there were around 15 to 20 people on the boat. Of them, 11, all minors aged around 15, have died. Seven people, including the boat owner, have been rescued. We are carrying out rescue operations, which will continue throughout the night,” Singh said.
Initial reports suggested that around 25 to 30 people were aboard the medium-sized boat, most of them travelling to attend a feast organised as part of Hindu funeral rituals.

news.story_lead: Five arrested as 29-year-old man dies after ‘assault’ over beer spill at north Delhi nightclub Police are examining CCTV footage and allegations of a firearm threat and theft as they investigate the death of Daljeet at Tor House nightclub. A probe into the death of a 29-year-old man following an alleged assault at a north Delhi nightclub has led to five arrests, including the establishment’s manager, his wife and three bouncers, police said on Tuesday. The incident occurred late on October 10 at Tor House, near Ashok Park Metro station in the Sarai Rohilla police station area.
news.full_article_text: Five arrested as 29-year-old man dies after ‘assault’ over beer spill at north Delhi nightclub Police are examining CCTV footage and allegations of a firearm threat and theft as they investigate the death of Daljeet at Tor House nightclub. A probe into the death of a 29-year-old man following an alleged assault at a north Delhi nightclub has led to five arrests, including the establishment’s manager, his wife and three bouncers, police said on Tuesday. The incident occurred late on October 10 at Tor House, near Ashok Park Metro station in the Sarai Rohilla police station area. The deceased, Daljeet, lived in Raghuvir Nagar with his wife, Pooja, their eight-year-old son and his father. Investigators are looking into a dispute that allegedly broke out after beer spilled on the club manager’s wife while Daljeet was at the venue with five to six friends, according to police. Also Read: 29-Year-Old Man Allegedly Beaten To Death By Club Bouncers Over Beer Spill Row | HT India The disagreement reportedly escalated when bouncers became involved. Daljeet’s friends alleged that the group apologised but was nevertheless attacked. They claimed the assault involved sticks and glass bottles and continued even after they asked the attackers to stop. The group also alleged that attempts to leave the premises were unsuccessful, with bouncers allegedly pulling them back inside and assaulting them again. Water was reportedly poured on the men during the incident. Daljeet suffered serious injuries, including a fractured jaw, his friends said. After managing to leave the club, his companions took him to his residence in Raghuvir Nagar. He collapsed near the entrance, according to the account provided by his friends, and was subsequently taken to Guru Gobind Singh Hospital , where doctors declared him dead. Sunny, one of Daljeet’s friends who sustained a minor head injury, said he received a call from Pooja following the incident. He alleged that footage of the assault was captured by the nightclub’s surveillance cameras and called for strict action against those involved. The group has raised other allegations, including that one of the accused displayed a firearm and that cash and two mobile phones were taken from them. Police are examining these claims as part of the ongoing investigation. Also Read: Woman allegedly stripped, beaten at Guwahati club after drunken brawl with bouncers To establish how the incident unfolded, investigators have taken possession of the nightclub’s digital video recorder (DVR) and are reviewing the CCTV footage. The exercise is also intended to help determine whether additional people were involved. The investigation is also examining a separate allegation by the family concerning the police response. The family claimed that a police response vehicle arrived outside the club after a call was made to the control room but left without conducting an inquiry. Police are additionally checking whether Tor House had the necessary permissions to operate late at night. Records have been sought from the Excise Department and the Licensing Branch in connection with the inquiry. Police are continuing to investigate the dispute, the alleged assault and the circumstances surrounding Daljeet’s death. news.full_article_text: Mangrove Army: How Sundarbans’ ‘tiger widows’ are protecting the forest, one sapling a time Known as the “Mangrove Army”, the group was recently praised by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his Mann Ki Baat address aired on September 27 An ‘army’ of women, many of whom have lost their husbands in tiger attacks, known as ‘tiger widows’, are now fighting to save the Sundarbans in West Bengal, the world’s largest mangrove delta and home to more than 100 tigers. Known as the “Mangrove Army”, the group was recently praised by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his Mann Ki Baat address aired on September 27. The women plant mangrove saplings along riverbanks to protect their villages from cyclones and help conserve the fragile ecosystem. Namita Kayal, 45, a resident of Lahiripur, a remote island in the Sundarbans, lost her husband to a tiger attack in 2021. He was killed while catching crabs in the creeks inside the forest. Her sister-in-law, Anita Kayal, lost her husband in a similar attack in 2017. The two women now work with the Mangrove Army, planting mangrove saplings along the riverbanks that separate their village from the forest inhabited by tigers. The group provides them with essential household supplies in return for their work. Also Read: Green tribunal impleads BMC in mangrove-dumping case in Diva “My sister-in-law and I have both lost our husbands in tiger attacks. They were the only earning members of our families. Now, we both work for the Mangrove Army. We receive ration and other items for planting mangroves on the muddy banks. There are many others in the group like us who have lost their husbands in tiger attacks,” Namita told HT over the phone. The group that is now called the ‘Mangrove Army’ was formed in 2009, after cyclone Aila devastated the Sundarbans, by Umashankar Mondal, a government schoolteacher in West Bengal. He brought together around 200 village women to plant mangrove saplings along riverbanks. Over the years, the initiative has grown to include around 600 women, of whom approximately 120 have lost their husbands in tiger attacks. “Since 2009, we have planted more than 1.3 million mangrove saplings along the riverbanks of 12 remote islands, including Satjelia, Kumirmari and Choto Mollakhali. We have been working silently all these years, away from the focus of mainstream media. It was only in July 2023 that we officially named the women’s group the ‘Mangrove Army’. It was recently highlighted by the Prime Minister,” said Mondal, secretary of the Purbasha Eco-helpline Society, the non-profit organisation behind the initiative. Also Read: 4.5-acre mangrove forest to make way for Tata Power switching station The women, ranging in age from 25 to over 60, wade through knee-deep mud along riverbanks to plant thousands of saplings every year. They do not receive wages for their work but are provided with essential supplies to support their families. “In return, we don’t get any money. Instead, we receive everyday items needed to run the family — rice, dal, cooking oil and spices. Sometimes, we also get sarees, sanitary napkins, seeds to grow vegetables, fish fingerlings for our ponds and chickens for poultry. Recently, the society organised free eye-testing camps, and those who needed spectacles were provided with them,” Anita said. In his Mann Ki Baat address, PM Modi praised the women for restoring the mangrove forests despite the personal losses they suffered. “In the Sundarbans of West Bengal, some women are setting an inspiring example of the special bond [that humans share] with nature. These women are growing and restoring mangrove forests. Many of these women lost their husbands in tiger attacks. After losing their husbands, they got support for their livelihood from the Sundarbans. The mangroves they had planted have now become a natural shield for the villages. They are also earning by planting these mangroves,” Modi said. Also Read: Sunderban crocodiles losing their nesting grounds due to climate change: Govt report The Sundarbans comprises around 102 islands, of which only 52 are inhabited. The remaining islands are home to national parks, tiger reserves and wildlife sanctuaries. The region is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Mangroves serve as a natural barrier against cyclones, helping protect coastal settlements from storm surges and strong winds. The Sundarbans also acts as a buffer for Kolkata, located around 100km to the northwest, against cyclones originating in the Bay of Bengal. However, the region’s mangrove cover remains vulnerable. Data from the Forest Survey of India (FSI) show that while the overall mangrove cover in the Sundarbans increased marginally between 2019 and 2021, the gains were largely driven by an expansion in open mangrove cover, which primarily includes plantations. According to the FSI’s 2021 report, the total mangrove cover in the Sundarbans, including very dense, moderately dense and open mangroves, increased from 2,112 sq km in 2019 to 2,114 sq km in 2021. The moderately dense mangrove cover remained unchanged during the period. Tiger attacks, meanwhile, continue to pose a risk to people who enter the forest to earn a living. Senior officials said such fatalities have declined over the years. At least 15 people were killed in tiger attacks in 2018, while no deaths were recorded in 2023 and one was reported in 2024. Some deaths may go unreported when villagers enter the forest without permission. For Namita, the Prime Minister’s recognition has brought long-awaited attention to the women’s efforts on the remote islands. “The Prime Minister himself flagged our work. It came as a huge achievement for us who work on the remote islands trying to save the Sundarbans and their villages,” she said. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Joydeep Thakur Joydeep Thakur is a Special Correspondent based in Kolkata. He focuses on science, environment, wildlife, agriculture and other related issues.

Now, we both work for the Mangrove Army. We receive ration and other items for planting mangroves on the muddy banks. There are many others in the group like us who have lost their husbands in tiger attacks,” Namita told HT over the phone. The group that is now called the ‘Mangrove Army’ was formed in 2009, after cyclone Aila devastated the Sundarbans, by Umashankar Mondal, a government schoolteacher in West Bengal. He brought together around 200 village women to plant mangrove saplings along riverbanks. Over the years, the initiative has grown to include around 600 women, of whom approximately 120 have lost their husbands in tiger attacks. “Since 2009, we have planted more than 1.3 million mangrove saplings along the riverbanks of 12 remote islands, including Satjelia, Kumirmari and Choto Mollakhali. We have been working silently all these years, away from the focus of mainstream media. It was only in July 2023 that we officially named the women’s group the ‘Mangrove Army’. It was recently highlighted by the Prime Minister,” said Mondal, secretary of the Purbasha Eco-helpline Society, the non-profit organisation behind the initiative. Also Read: 4.5-acre mangrove forest to make way for Tata Power switching station The women, ranging in age from 25 to over 60, wade through knee-deep mud along riverbanks to plant thousands of saplings every year. They do not receive wages for their work but are provided with essential supplies to support their families. “In return, we don’t get any money. Instead, we receive everyday items needed to run the family — rice, dal, cooking oil and spices. Sometimes, we also get sarees, sanitary napkins, seeds to grow vegetables, fish fingerlings for our ponds and chickens for poultry. Recently, the society organised free eye-testing camps, and those who needed spectacles were provided with them,” Anita said. In his Mann Ki Baat address, PM Modi praised the women for restoring the mangrove forests despite the personal losses they suffered. “In the Sundarbans of West Bengal, some women are setting an inspiring example of the special bond [that humans share] with nature. These women are growing and restoring mangrove forests. Many of these women lost their husbands in tiger attacks. After losing their husbands, they got support for their livelihood from the Sundarbans. The mangroves they had planted have now become a natural shield for the villages. They are also earning by planting these mangroves,” Modi said. The remaining islands are home to national parks, tiger reserves and wildlife sanctuaries. The region is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Mangroves serve as a natural barrier against cyclones, helping protect coastal settlements from storm surges and strong winds. The Sundarbans also acts as a buffer for Kolkata, located around 100km to the northwest, against cyclones originating in the Bay of Bengal. However, the region’s mangrove cover remains vulnerable. Data from the Forest Survey of India (FSI) show that while the overall mangrove cover in the Sundarbans increased marginally between 2019 and 2021, the gains were largely driven by an expansion in open mangrove cover, which primarily includes plantations. According to the FSI’s 2021 report, the total mangrove cover in the Sundarbans, including very dense, moderately dense and open mangroves, increased from 2,112 sq km in 2019 to 2,114 sq km in 2021. The moderately dense mangrove cover remained unchanged during the period. Tiger attacks, meanwhile, continue to pose a risk to people who enter the forest to earn a living. Senior officials said such fatalities have declined over the years. At least 15 people were killed in tiger attacks in 2018, while no deaths were recorded in 2023 and one was reported in 2024. Some deaths may go unreported when villagers enter the forest without permission. It came as a huge achievement for us who work on the remote islands trying to save the Sundarbans and their villages,” she said. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Joydeep Thakur Joydeep Thakur is a Special Correspondent based in Kolkata. news.full_article_text: India's opposition party members march to the Supreme Court in protest against a controversial revision of voter lists that has sparked days of unrest, in Delhi - Published 12 October 2026 Thousands of opposition supporters marched through Delhi to India's Supreme Court to demand the election chief resign over alleged electoral roll fraud. Monday's "March for Democracy" was the latest in a series of demonstrations, with thousands of security forces deployed and roads barricaded in the capital. Thousands of protesters were detained over the weekend. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi submitted a petition to the court challenging the process, in which tens of millions of names have been struck off the voter rolls. Opposition parties allege the revision benefits Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The Election Commission and the BJP reject the charge. For weeks requests to protest had been denied by police, citing law and order reasons. Attempts to hold a protest by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) pressure group over the weekend led to thousands of demonstrators being detained in Delhi. Gandhi called "all opposition parties, civil society groups [and] all those who believe in democracy" to join Monday's march. In a press conference, he shared a letter that he and Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge had written to Chief Justice Surya Kant, laying out their concerns with Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's alleged conduct. After they filed their petition later in the day, Kant responded by saying the matter was already before the court and therefore sub judice - meaning he could not speak about it. But he added: "You have my assurance that any such petition shall be heard at the earliest possible opportunity, in accordance with the law." There was a heavy security deployment in central Delhi and along the route of the march, with restrictions on traffic and on entry and exit at some metro stations. A bus carrying Gandhi and other opposition leaders made its way to the court from Barakamba road. Supporters waved flags and chanted his name as the Congress MP and others waved through the windows. Seated a few rows behind him was Neha Bora, a student leader who has gained prominence in the protests. A few kilometres on, in a place called Mandi House, the bus stopped and Rahul Gandhi and a few others climbed on top of the vehicle to wave at supporters lining up the street in the thousands. Many protesters climbed on to other buses parked here, while some waved flags and chanted anti-government slogans to the sound of drums and lots of cheering. "If they take away our right to vote, what is left with us?" one protester asked an AFP news agency reporter. Another protester called the march "a fight to save the very fabric" of India, the world's largest democracy. Main opposition leader Rahul Gandhi holds up a copy of India's Constitution at a press conference on Monday Protesters have been demanding the country's the election chief resign over alleged electoral roll fraud Over the past week, top opposition leaders, including Gandhi, have been briefly detained several times while leading protests in central Delhi. On Sunday, the CJP - which is not a registered political party - said it would continue protesting until Kumar stepped down. The CJP, which successfully led a protest over the summer that culminated in India's federal education minister's resignation, had called for a march on Saturday to Jantar Mantar - the best-known protest site in Delhi where the last set of sit-in demonstrations had also happened. But authorities in Delhi imposed overarching restrictions that made it almost impossible for protesters to travel and reach Jantar Mantar - trains were cancelled, dozens of metro stations were shut and tens of thousands of police and paramilitary personnel were on the roads to detain protesters. The Home Ministry has now announced demonstrations will no longer be permitted at Jantar Mantar. Three other sites have been listed as alternatives should permission be granted. Monday's demonstrations come after thousands were detained over the weekend The CJP leaders - founder Abhijeet Dipke and co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka - were dramatically detained from a plane as they landed in Delhi to join the weekend protest. They were only released a day later - while Dipke returned home to attend his grandmother's funeral, Das and Ranka held a press conference where they said the protests would continue. Both leaders have said they will seek a new protest date from the police. Over the weekend, the police detained and released thousands of people, including several journalists. Some videos and photos from the protest show police dragging people, including women, by force and pushing them into buses. The BBC also captured footage , external of a policeman slapping a detained protester inside a bus. The Delhi police did not respond to questions about the use of violence against protesters. In a statement, Reporters Without Borders condemned the detention of at least 16 Indian journalists. "Covering events of public interest is not a crime. It is their job. The police's actions against the press are unacceptable," it said. Rahul Gandhi said that young Indians who had come to peacefully protest with "love in their hearts, not hatred or anger" had been beaten up. BJP President Nitin Nabin accused opposition parties and the CJP of trying to destabilise India "at the behest of foreign forces" without elaborating on who the forces were. Related topics

news.full_article_text: Odisha Cabinet approves free textbooks for 28.7 lakh students, ₹500-crore urban drainage scheme Odisha Cabinet approves free textbooks for 28.7 lakh students, ₹ 500-crore urban drainage scheme Bhubaneswar, Oct13 The Odisha government on Tuesday approved free textbooks for around 28.7 lakh students of state-run schools, along with a ₹ 500-crore programme to improve urban drainage and tackle flooding. The decisions were among 16 proposals approved at a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi here. The proposals, relating to 11 departments, will be implemented soon, Chief Secretary Anu Garg told reporters after the meeting. The decision to provide free textbooks to more students comes amid a controversy over the supply of textbooks containing errors, with opposition parties demanding the resignation of School and Mass Education Minister Nityananda Gond. Garg said students of classes 9 and 10 in government and government-aided secondary schools, other than those covered under the existing SC and ST provisions, would now receive free textbooks. The scheme aims to ensure equitable access to quality education, reduce the financial burden on economically weaker families, improve enrolment in government schools, lower dropout rates and increase the transition from elementary to secondary education. Students belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes were already receiving free textbooks, she said. "The scheme will remain in force for five years, from 2025-26 to 2029-30, with a total estimated outlay of ₹ 284.07 crore, covering a tentative 28.7 lakh beneficiaries," Garg said. The procurement of paper, printing, transportation and distribution of textbooks will be undertaken through a transparent and competitive process in accordance with the Odisha General Financial Rules and applicable procurement guidelines, she said. The School and Mass Education Department will put in place a mechanism to collect, verify and validate beneficiary data through field-level verification. It will also ensure that textbooks are printed and supplied to schools well before the commencement of each academic session, Garg said. Over 1,600 mistakes, including spelling errors and incorrect names of eminent personalities, were found in 55 textbooks supplied by the department. In another major decision, the Cabinet approved the Urban Storm Water Drainage Management and Improvement Programme , with an outlay of ₹ 500 crore from the state's own resources over a period of five years, from 2026-27 to 2030-31. The scheme will cover urban local bodies and selected block headquarters. The proposed interventions include desilting, construction of reinforced cement concrete stormwater drains, covering of drains, restoration of natural drainage channels and their linkage with suitable water bodies. The measures are aimed at improving the capacity and efficiency of urban drainage systems and reducing waterlogging and localised flooding, Garg said. The programme is also expected to promote groundwater recharge, improve public safety and environmental quality, and support climate-resilient urban development. The Cabinet also approved the establishment of a Disaster Recovery-cum-Data Centre at Keonjhar to ensure the uninterrupted functioning of critical government digital services during major disruptions, including earthquakes and cyclones. The Odisha State Data Centre in Bhubaneswar hosts critical government applications, databases and platforms supporting government-to-government, government-to-business and government-to-citizen services. The proposed facility at Keonjhar will serve as a disaster recovery centre, enabling the state to protect its data and maintain essential services in the event of a major disruption at the Bhubaneswar facility. "Both Keonjhar and Bhubaneswar are located in different seismic zones. If there is any damage in Bhubaneswar, data could remain safe at the Keonjhar centre," Garg said. The project will cost over ₹ 176 crore, including capital expenditure of ₹ 154 crore and operational expenditure of ₹ 22.83 crore for five years. An amount of ₹ 162.83 crore has been provided from the Fifth State Finance Commission grant-in-aid, she said. The state Cabinet also approved a tender worth ₹ 105 crore for the construction of an in-stream water storage project on the Tel river at Tustapali village in Bolangir district. The project is expected to strengthen water security and help mitigate chronic water scarcity in the drought-prone district. Apart from these proposals, the Cabinet approved measures relating to the Fisheries and Animal Resources Development; Industries, Skill Development and Technical Education; Finance; Electronics and Information Technology; Agriculture and Farmers' Empowerment; Housing and Urban Development; Revenue and Disaster Management; Water Resources; and School and Mass Education departments.
